utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. I was advised, Mr. Karadzic, that you have something to raise before the witness enters the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Excellencies. Good afternoon, everybody. Yes, I've asked for a short time to be allotted me to present what I have, better in the absence of the witness. This has to do with associated evidentiary cases; i.e., exhibits. You have been [indiscernible] inclined to this possibility towards me. Namely, I have not been given 48 hours for this witness, and there are many things which are repetitive, but they are not identical. They confirm certain events. And, therefore, I should like to ask you how I am to proceed. My proposal is that you ask the witness to take a look at a number of documents and at a number of agency pieces of news which have to do with the government, the activities of the government. There are some statements of his there as well. There are some statements of the government which we do not have, as such, but which have been communicated via agencies. There are various notices of vacancies for prison guards, et cetera. So no comments, in fact, but just news, pieces of news that the witness is aware of, and events, developments, that the witness is aware of. I should like to ask the Chamber that the witness look at these and then initial the documents in question, and then the parties, together with the Chamber, could decide what is to be done with them. And I should also like to hear the stance of the other party on this issue. There would be [indiscernible] a number of other governmental documents, because what I want us to do is not to repeat documents which are similar in nature to those that we have already seen and shown, but they are important for gaining the full picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Question number 1, Mr. Karadzic: Has the witness seen those documents yet?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we have had no contacts with the witness. Had we known that it would be a Chamber witness, we would have taken those steps, but I meant, actually, for the Chamber to ask the witness to take a look in the afternoon -- or, rather, in his spare time. This is not much. These are merely agency news. He hasn't seen these documents yet, but he knows of the events which they depict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Second question is, Mr. Karadzic, whether the Prosecution has been informed of the list of documents you want to tender in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, since I have been given 48 -- had I been given 48 hours, I would have actually presented these documents myself. But since I haven't been allotted that much time, I thought that we should proceed in this way: by the witness examining the documents, and then we should like to ask the other side, the Prosecution, to actually state their position on what the witness states. It goes without saying that this can be, of course, rejected or dismissed, but what is of the essence is for the witness to finish his part of the job while he is here, and it is then up to us to either admit or not admit some of those pieces of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just let me be clear. So the Prosecution at this moment does not have a clue what documents you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That heard, I have to ask you, Mr. Tieger, what would you say to this suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A couple of things, Your Honour. First of all, Dr. Karadzic raised this earlier, as, I believe, the Chamber will recall, and was told at that time to present the documents to the Prosecution so the process could move forward. As a general matter, we -- the Prosecution agrees that there are expeditious ways of presenting relevant documents, and we're happy to seek, with the Defence, an appropriate -- any appropriate mechanism of doing so. And, in general, had we been presented with these documents, we would have treated it as an anticipated Bar table submission and dealt with the documents accordingly. So it's unfortunate that that process was not followed. As I understand the current suggestion, it seems to be an amalgamation of several different approaches, kind of combining the normal process of presenting documents to a witness with a classical Bar table submission. I anticipated, when the accused raised the possibility earlier and was advised by the Court to present them to the Prosecution, that we would be dealing with them as a Bar table submission, and we were quite prepared to do so and to be wholly amenable to that process. I'm not quite sure I understand the sort of combined process the accused is now suggesting. But as the Court notes, we're not aware of what those documents are, so we're rather in the dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is a bit different from an ordinary Bar table motion is that in this case, we can have a witness's confirmation, albeit in brief form.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, as the Court noted, it's one thing to confirm a document, and that's more along the lines of a kind of 92 ter process, documents that the witness produced himself, so that's a document from the Ministry of Justice bearing my signature. That's a rather perfunctory process which often accompanies a witness's testimony, and which, by the way, up to now, we've had some trouble getting into evidence without a formal 92 ter process. I'm not saying we have to proceed that way, but I am just noting that that has been the case. But I also note that Dr. Karadzic appears to be suggesting the presentation of documents to the witness which really don't have any relationship to him. I understand he's talking about newspaper articles, about general events and so on, and I don't think a simple review by the witness and some sort of signal that he's familiar with the general events advances the process. I think it could be far more useful to the Chamber if those documents were presented, both parties could identify the relevance or authenticity issues surrounding that document, and they could proceed in the fashion that has been adopted in many other cases, and I think it is quite useful so the Court knows the relevance and knows whether or not there are any authenticity issues as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I would like also to take this opportunity to hear from you regarding the accused's suggestion to tender parts of Mr. Mandic's testimony in Stanisic and Zupljanin pursuant to Rule 92 ter. I take it you also received the list of pages he wished to tender in that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We did, Your Honour, and I, frankly, didn't give thought to responding. I understood that the Court had made a decision on that, and we simply reviewed the material -- the pages identified to see whether there were additional pages from those transcripts that we considered should also be submitted, and we identified a handful of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Tieger. Did you say that the Court had made a decision on that? What decision do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I understood that the -- as I recall the backdrop to this issue, the matter was raised by the accused. We had some discussion about the 92 ter process generally, which tended to focus on the more classical form of reviewing the transcripts and then the acknowledgment by the Chamber that this witness had been before this Court very recently -- not this Court, but had been to the Tribunal very recently, and that appeared to be a step which was unnecessary, but the Court simply invited the accused, rather than submitting the entirety of the transcript, to review it for those particular sections that he wanted. So when we received his identification of the portions that he wanted, we reviewed the entirety of the transcripts ourselves to identify any additional pages that we would ask the Court to admit along with those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Actually, I don't think the Chamber has made a final decision on this matter. But I take it that you do not object to tendering those parts into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. Our position is that the 92 ter process is, of course, available, and provided that the Court is satisfied that the conditions are met. And, as I say, I think we identified the only issue that appeared to be -- or the only matter that appeared potentially to be at issue, and I understand the Court was satisfied it was not, at least in this particular circumstance. So we certainly don't have any objection to both sides availing themselves of 92 ter when appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. The Chamber will rule on the admissibility in due course very soon, Mr. Karadzic. But when a Chamber receives as evidence some part of the transcript, it is often receiving the exhibit which is associated with that transcript which forms an indispensable or an inseparable part of that transcript. So are you going to tender some exhibit under that regime, as associated exhibit, whether you can identify some exhibit under that category?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And whether we grant your suggestion or not, I think I recommend you to immediately disclose the list of documents, together with the 65 ter numbers, to the Prosecution so that they can respond to your suggestion, which does not form an inseparable, indispensable part of the transcript. There's one further matter I'd like to visit before we begin the hearing of evidence. Last week, we informed the parties informally, on Friday last week, that a maximum of four hours would be permitted for cross-examination of the next scheduled witness, i.e., KDZ-272 or Mr. Milan Mandilovic. The Chamber's assessment was made on the basis of the criteria we have set out previously and, in particular, Mr. Karadzic's own estimate of the time needed for cross-examination, the Prosecution's estimate of the time needed for direct examination, the witness's amalgamated statement, and the scope and subject matter of the witness's anticipated evidence. In light of that assessment, the Chamber was of the view that a maximum of four hours is a reasonable time to the accused's cross-examination of Mr. Mandilovic. Thank you. That said, we'll bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, one more matter, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I can have one second to check an issue with Mr. Reid. Your Honour, again this is a scheduling matter, and I appreciate the Court's assistance on these issues. As the Court will recall, when we requested the projected cross-examination time, it was in connection with the scheduling of the upcoming witnesses. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who is supposed to come on Monday, the 19th?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, it's still Mr. -- we still have Mr. Mandilovic after Mr. Mandic, and then Mr. Abdel-Razek. But the witness afterwards we indicated was going to be Mr. Mole, and the reason was we had hoped to fill in the smallish slot available, that is, the limited time available after Mr. Abdel-Razek, with the witness, who wouldn't have to go back and forth, and so we shifted the schedule lighting so Mr. Soljevic, who was projected for a longer period of time, would not be required to come back and forth, and hopefully we could complete a witness. As it turns out, Mr. Mole was not available, so we need to revert back to the original schedule, which has Mr. Soljevic following Mr. Abdel-Razek. So the schedule will be Mr. Mandilovic, Mr. Abdel-Razek, and then Mr. Soljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the information. Mr. Karadzic, in the meantime, when do you think you can prepare the compilation of documents to be put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, most of it, especially the agency news part, is something I could submit to the OTP today, although my idea had been first to have my idea verified and then to see whether it is admissible or not, because I do not know whether Mr. Mandic will leave in the meantime, whether, in other words, he will be able to examine all these documents after we have reached agreement with the OTP. I thought that Mr. Mandic could do so today and tomorrow in his spare time and to initial the documents that he's familiar with, and then the two sides could agree on what portion of these documents is admissible or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you do that, the Chamber wants to see that list of documents as soon as possible, and that should be disclosed to the Prosecution in advance as well. Good afternoon, Mr. Mandic. I hope you had a refreshing weekend and you had a safe journey. Mr. Tieger, did you have something?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I can raise it -- I think I understand the proposal a little better, and it prompted a comment, but we can deal with that once we receive a list in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you, Mr. Minister.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good fortune to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D02095. This is a government document, an excerpt from instructions for the work of crisis staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, let me ask you this: Was the government delighted at the chaos which was obtaining or was it in desperation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government was extremely worried over what was going on in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Namely, some experts of the OTP suggest that the crimes which were being committed in our civil war were something that the government favoured, it favoured such a course of developments, or in the very least it did not exert any efforts to stop that, and those with the most extreme anti-Serbian orientation actually claim that this is what the government wanted. So the question is: If the government really had wanted that, would not it have been glad at what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government was doing everything in its power, when all the communications in the field had been severed, both road communications and telecommunications, to prevent any developments that were detrimental to both the Serbian and the Muslim and the Croat people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that last time we established that the Serbian crisis staffs were activated on the 4th of April, after the proclamation of general mobilisation which had been declared by the Croat and Muslim portion of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this. This is the 1st of May, 1992 -- sorry. No, in fact, it was the 26th of April. You were still formally in the MUP. You were not yet a minister of justice. Can you read the title and item 1?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Excerpt from the instruction for the work of the municipality crisis staffs of the Serbian people." Item 1: "In a state of war, the Crisis Staff shall take over all the prerogatives and functions of the municipal assemblies, when they are unable to convene."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree when there is a heavy snowfall or when there are floods or when there is no heat and gas, namely, in any situation which requires the intensive action of the authorities, crisis staffs would be -- or were established?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page in Serbian, and I believe it is the same page in English, which starts with item 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read items 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "9. The Crisis Staff shall create conditions for the work of the international peace-making and humanitarian organisations and ensure the safe passage of humanitarian aid convoys to their final destinations. "10. Treat extremely humanely and in accordance with the International Red Cross towards the non-combat populace and the wounded, and act humanely and in accordance with the laws of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina towards the POWs."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now also read item 13, and the rest is available to the participants for them to read if they so wish.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 13: "War profiteers, looting mobs and the like, are to be arrested and handed over to the investigating judicial organs of the Serbian republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are aware of these efforts of the government; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about this earlier, when I was examined here by both the Prosecutor as well as you, yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D407, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, would it be fair to say that we, at the central level, had remained without anything and that we started creating our state from scratch? As they now put it, it was a green field enterprise?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have confirmed this many times, and when I talked about the Ministry of Justice, I said that I didn't even have a pencil or paper, let alone anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A witness had confirmed to us here that two years would have been required to set up an army, whereas we did not have a witness who would have told us how much time would have been required for the creation of a proper state in conditions of poverty, sanctions, war. Could you say how much time is required for the setting up of a proper state administration?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I was minister of justice for about eight months, and I did not manage to establish that ministry, and then I left that position. I mean, I didn't manage to do it fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to see the vacancy announcements that you had. We'll see that later on. You asked for people who had passed the Bar exam to apply. Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2097, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a document that was created three days later. Do we now -- yes, we do have a translation. So could you please have a look at this document. It's the government and the Ministry for Health, Social Welfare, and Family Affairs. They are sending this to all crisis staffs, under the authority issued by the government. Do you remember who the minister of health was?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Dragan Kalinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- I do apologise to the interpreters. Do you agree that Mr. Kalinic before the war was a reformist in Ante Markovic's party and that he headed that club of MPs in Parliament?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that he and Dragan Cukanovic and others, other officials, were in the government, although they were not members of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, could you have a look at this now? Could you read, for instance, the first paragraph and the first sentence of paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To all regional crisis staffs. "Under the authority from the President of the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we are issuing the following instructions concerning humanitarian aid and actions which are being taken on the territories under the control of your staff. "1. We ask you to provide free passage to all convoys of humanitarian aid (food, clothes, medicaments, sanitary material) being transported through the areas under your control, regardless of whether these convoys are organised by international or domestic humanitarian organisations."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read on the same paragraph: "That pertains to ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "That pertains to all convoys, regardless of their destination of the localities that can be under your control or under the control of the Muslim or Croatian authorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go on, number 2?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2: "You are required to make it clear to all heads of medical facilities on your territory, both civilian and military ones, to continue treating the sick and wounded, regardless of their ethnicity and political beliefs, in accordance with the basic principles of medical ethics, and all patients should be given medical treatment of the same quality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 3, just the first sentence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3: "As regards the treatment of prisoners of war, internationally established norms must be respected concerning their accommodation, nutrition, and medical treatment."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree -- or do you remember, Minister, that the Presidency, on the 13th of June, issued a set of instructions in terms of treating POWs, and Minister Subotic drafted that? It was my order, I signed it, but the instructions had to do with the card that he provided, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You gave instructions as to how they should be treated, and within that you ordered, inter alia, that the minister for military affairs issue instructions regarding the treatment of POWs with the force of decree or, rather, with the force of law, because this published in the Official Gazette. Therefore, it had the force of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that that order was almost unnecessary, because we see that on the 27th of April, before I even became a member of the Presidency, the minister of health had already taken a measure along those lines and issued instructions to regional crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was necessary, because there was not sufficient co-ordination between the local level and the central authorities. At that point, the government that was still being established had very poor communication with the local level, and I believe that it was indispensable to have something like this done, from the point of view of -- well, I mean, that such a thing would come from the Presidency or the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe you're right as far as the local level is concerned. But from the point of view of the central government and central authorities, was that indispensable, because we see that they functioned along those lines even without that order and instructions having been issued?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, the government took all sorts of measures in order to prevent the violation of international norms and violations of human rights. However, since that was not sufficient, you also took certain measures from the domain of your own powers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, this document was an instruction, signed by the minister of health and social welfare, to the regional crisis headquarters, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why, then, was it written in English at the time? I see the original was in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance? There is an original in Serbian too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's hear from the witness first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't even look at this English version. However, I assumed that there was an original in Serbian. I mean, Dr. Kalinic does speak English, but I think that all documents of the government were written in the Serbian language, without a single exception. You will have to see, with Mr. Kalinic, why he did this in English. I imagine it was for the benefit of international factors, international humanitarian organisations, who were already moving about Bosnia-Herzegovina that was at war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, Minister, whether any humanitarian organisation could have had this on them if they were moving about in the field, and if they were to come across certain obstacles, could they have this as a kind of pass or something?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they knew this -- that they used this document as a pass. I know that you issued an order to the police and judiciary and military organs to allow unhindered passage to all international and local humanitarian organisations in the territory that was under Serb control at that time. There was an order of yours to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that it exists both in an English version and in a Serbian version, and that the English version was being carried around by these humanitarians? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. President, I just saw these Serbian versions at government meetings and in the Official Gazette, and in other trials when I testified; Stanisic, Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you that they asked me not to put a date so that no one could say, at local level, that it was out of date or something, would you be surprised?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a matter to be agreed upon, but I remember full well that the government and the central authorities of Republika Srpska were trying to find the best possible ways to ensure unhindered passage to all humanitarian organisations held -- in territories held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It will be Exhibit D408.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, you're a lawyer, a judge. You are familiar with the Constitution and legislation. Do you agree that according to our Constitution, the president did not have to attend Assembly sessions at all, unless he is presenting an expose of his own or if he is invited?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is MPs and the president of the Assembly that have to attend Assembly meetings. Certain representatives of the executive or from the Presidency may attend if the subjects dealt with -- fall within the scope of their own work or if they're invited by the MPs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put a pause before you start answering the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 156, that's the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. This is a record of the session of the National Security Council and the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, let me ask you: Do you recall that at the time, all the way up until the 12th of May, the Assembly was not in a position to meet?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until there was a corridor in place in Posavina, it was practically impossible to move from Western to Eastern Herzegovina or from Central Bosnia to Eastern Bosnia. There were obstacles on the roads, and all other links of communication were extremely difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that after Assembly life came into being, the National Security Council practically ceased to exist and function?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this National Security Council, I know very little about it. I think that it is actually something that goes beyond the Constitution. This was a provisional organ before the Presidency was established, and perhaps even the Assembly too. I really don't know what the role of this council was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, you do recall that the Assembly and the president can establish advisory bodies and that that is in line with the Constitution?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that this council was supposed to support the government until proper Assembly life started, and that after that, the government worked with the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 7, subparagraph A. Could you please read that? As for all the participants in these proceedings, they have the entire document made available to them.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "7. It was decided to prepare and propose to the Assembly that it adopt the following:" Which subparagraph did you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subparagraph A: "A list of laws which should be adopted within three months. These laws secure the functioning of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 8: "Appropriate ministers should stand in for directors of public funds before they are appointed." No, I beg your pardon. Number 8 reads as follows: "The State Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War and the Dead was appointed."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that was the 8th, and then it was confirmed on the 10th; right? Can we have page 3 now. You were elected two days later, you became a member of the government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 12th of May, at the session of the Assembly of the Serb People in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you to read subparagraph F?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "F. To take necessary measures to bring together professionals and ensure conditions for the work of state and judicial organs."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So a month after the outbreak of the war, there weren't enough trained personnel, and one of the items on the agenda is to try to find appropriate personnel. And we'll see later on in the media that all persons who had passed the Bar examination were called upon to report. Thank you. So could this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D409, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 65 ter 162, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to tell us what this is all about? What is this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes from the government meeting held on the 24th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you not find it striking that there is no more National Security Council?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 2.1, can you read that sentence, and can you interpret it for us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.1: "It has been determined that the Ministry of the Interior should prepare a comprehensive analysis for the government regarding the security situation and the state of law and order in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please go on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The question of crime should be dealt with, in particular, as well as the protection of private and social property, mistreatment of citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as other questions that are important as regards the status of people in the Serb republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 now, could you read that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3: "It was agreed --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 3, and then subparagraph 3 as well.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3(3): "It was concluded that the overall situation in the republic should be recorded as soon as possible. To that end, groups of ministers would be formed which would have direct insight in various municipalities and would prepare reports and suggest measures to be undertaken."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Minister, does that mean that the government, on the 24th of May, did not have insight into what was going on in the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D410, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you about something else, an event that you attended to. Do you remember that on the 12th of May, I was elected to the Presidency and to the position of president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of the B and H?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it was published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the Police Academy in Banja Luka staged a ceremony that we attended on the 13th of May?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th -- actually, the 13th of May was the Police Day for 50 years in the former Yugoslavia, and the Serbs were the only ones who kept fostering that tradition and celebrating the 13th of May. And there was a central show, a central event, in the Police Academy in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, someone has suggested to the OTP that we intended to part ways with the Muslims living in the territories that the Serbs were claiming as theirs. We were always very explicit. We said that if Bosnia was to leave the joint state, we wanted to part from the majority parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina in order to avoid what the Muslims wished to avoid in Yugoslavia; namely, that position of a minority. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the proposal of the international community, of Cutileiro's Plan. He actually -- he actually proposed this in order to avoid out-voting in all institutions at all government levels in Bosnia and Herzegovina. According to Cutileiro's Plan, the Lisbon Agreement and the Sarajevo Agreement, there should have been three entities in one state. And initially the Serb and the Muslim and the Croat sides all agreed to that, but subsequently, at someone's instructions, the Serbs remained -- adhered to this agreement, but the Croats and Muslims didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you at this event in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because my brother was a director there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see an insert -- a piece of footage from that event at the academy on the 13th of May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we stop there? We're supposed to hear the interpretation, based upon this circulated document, so shall we begin again? I take it this document was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 2090. That is the transcript of the part that we're interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to ask the interpreters whether they have been provided with this translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have, but I cannot hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a translation. I have it here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters also have the translation. It is just that we cannot follow the footage, because I cannot hear a single word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I heard some Serbian in the video-clip, but the interpreters said that they didn't hear anything from this footage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neither can I, neither can I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that at this event there were Muslims and Croats, and that I welcomed that fact, and that my welcoming of that fact was responded to by applause on the part of all present?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we should like to see that and to hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's give it a try again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that perhaps they will be able to fix it after the break. Anyway, I owe you this video-clip, and then after the break, when it has been dealt with, we shall submit it. There is one page of the speech which I delivered, where I congratulate the Muslims and the Croats, and I say that we are not in conflict with Muslims and Croats, but only with the militant leaderships of the two communities. Can we now have 65 ter 165. And after the break, we shall be satisfied that this is so and see the video-clip itself. 65 ter 165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Sanction should stop. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that the government was not too happy and exactly satisfied with the crisis staffs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as I can recall, there was an initiative launched by the government for them to be abolished; the crisis staffs, namely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this because they were unable to exercise power and the government had no way of controlling them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the majority of cases, they were unable to govern the situation in the field, to control the situation in the field, or they did wrongly what they had been tasked to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document, and tell us, was it the case that on the 31st of May, the government was abolishing the crisis staffs; right? This is the 31st of May; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 17th Session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 1(b) is a decision on the setting up of War Presidencies in the municipalities; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that corresponds to what I recollect; namely, that the government proposed that municipal crisis staffs should be dismantled.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 2. I believe it is page 2 in the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 4, can you read that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 4 -- in Article 4: "Add a new third paragraph which were foresee that the republican commissioner can be authorised for a number of municipalities according to, if so possible, the organisation of the Army of the Serbian Republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next one, the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Add a new article after Article 4, the fifth article, which would foresee the abolishment of crisis staffs in municipalities with the setting up of a War Presidency."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Karadzic. Could you draw our attention to the passage which deals with the dismantling of municipal crisis staffs? I don't think I saw that passage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is directly above "AD-2" or "Re. 2."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 15, can you please read the second paragraph? In English, it is also the next page -- actually, the page with "Item 15" on it. Another page, please. Yes, and yet another page. In English, it is on the top of the page, and here it is 15, item 15, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "Regarding this issue, it has been established that the government is not sufficiently informed about issues relevant to its work, in particular, the situation on the front. It has been concluded that the government must be regularly informed about said issues through the Ministry of Defence, the Main Staff, and the Ministry of the Interior in order to be able to, within its rights and powers, engage on the formulation of policy and adoption of positions, coming up with appropriate solutions and their realisation."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this yet more proof that the government is groping in the dark, as it were, and that it is unable to control -- to manage processes?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D411, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D2098.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, we see "Current Issues," item 17: [In English] "It has been agreed that Mr. Subic, the husband of Mrs. Rabija Subic, should accompany the humanitarian aid convoy." Can you tell the Chamber, what was -- what is Rabija Subic by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One witness actually said that Rabija Subic was a Serbian nationalist. Would you agree that this was a modern Muslim woman of a pro-European and pro-Yugoslav orientation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the majority of Muslims had been who lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina up to this war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that she's married to Mlade [phoen] Subic, who is named after a Croatian king and who comes from an eminent Croatian family?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Mlade Subic, this Croat also was a pro-Yugoslav -- of a pro-Yugoslav and pro-European orientation. Do you agree that Rabija Subic was the president of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The interpreter did not hear the end of Mr. Karadzic's question, previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, interpreters noted that they didn't hear the end of your last question. But, by the way, are you dealing with this document which is before us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. and Mrs. Subic were in the previous document, and I just noticed, and I wished Mr. Mandic to tell us that Rabija Subic was not at all any kind of a Serbian nationalist, and that the expert witness who said so actually misinterpreted things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, can you take a look at this supplement to the decision, which I signed on the 31st of May, 1992, amendment on the establishment, seat, and jurisdiction of military courts and military prosecutors' offices. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we have said, so far there was a military judiciary and a civilian judiciary. This is an addition to an existing document. It was a decision. It was amended on the 31st of May; namely, the decision on the establishment, seat, and jurisdiction of military courts and military prosecutorial offices. And I believe that it refers to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and the seat of the prosecutorial office attached to that corps.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap. The interpreter is unable to follow. I didn't hear Mr. Karadzic's question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. You should note the interpreter's note again. Because of your overlapping, the interpreters couldn't follow you at all. Could you repeat your last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was: Do you remember that initially both the courts and the prosecutors' offices were attached to strategic groups, namely, to the corps and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, and I was versed in the subject-matter, every corps had its own prosecutors' office and its own judiciary, and the supreme military court and the leadership of the military judiciary was attached to the Main Staff in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree or do you remember that later I removed the courts to the Ministry of Defence, while leaving the prosecutorial offices in the army, and that I had some complaints regarding that move of mine?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the proposal of the minister of defence, you did so, and there was a falling-out between you and the chief of the General Staff, Mr. Ratko Mladic, on that occasion and in that connection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D412, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 167 now, please. Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at this, please. It's the 19th Session of the government, held on the 2nd of June, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read item 1, up to "it was concluded that ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "1. The government has considered current issues in the work of the government and the ministries. "It has been concluded that the necessary measures for the rehabilitation of the complete social and economic life everywhere on the territory of the republic should be introduced and undertaken even faster than now. "The need to revive economic activities has been especially emphasised. With regard to that, the importance of establishing the road network that would connect all the regions of the republic has been emphasised again, with a special emphasis on the basic corridors connecting the Bosnian Krajina to Semberija, SAO Romanija, and East Herzegovina to Semberija," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can skip the next part and read: "It was concluded ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It was concluded that all the ministries should speed up the drafting and propose the laws from their portfolios that would provide functioning of the economy, the government, and would ensure the rule of law."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the next passage?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Instances of robberies or looting of even the Serbian people have been emphasised as a particular problem. It has, therefore, been pointed out that all the measures to prevent that should be undertaken."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government once again --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government once again concluded that it is not informed about current political and military issues and about the situation in the republic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this shows that the government was only issuing documents, with no way of implementing them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I was speaking metaphorically. I thought that the government was in a vacuum.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the existence of road and telegraph communications?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that at the beginning, when I said that at the beginning of the war, all the roads in Bosnia and Herzegovina were blocked, obstructed, those held -- those in parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina held by the Serbs as well as those held by the Muslims or the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the second paragraph in Serbian: "It was concluded that ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It was concluded that the government should be informed on these issues every day and that this should be the first item on the agenda. "To make this possible, there has to be constant direct contact with the Main Staff, through the prime minister and the minister of defence, and a quality communications system between the state organs and the military commander should be provided. "All this entails examination of the current locations of the highest government bodies and the military command."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the next?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The problem of the lack of army officers has been brought up at the meeting. This is one of the most important and urgent problems the government should deal with."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe to Their Honours and everybody in the courtroom what the premises of the government organs at Kikinda, Pale, and other places looked like?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony so far, I said something that is confirmed by these minutes. The ministers were informed only from the prime minister about events on the ground, and he received his information either from the Main Staff or other people. And when the war broke out, the government was located on temporary premises. The name of the building was Kikinda. This was on the outskirts of Pale. And then some 10 or 15 kilometres away, in Hotel Bistrica at Jahorina. This hotel had been built for the Olympic Games in 1984. We did not have the proper conditions for our work in that hotel. For example, my ministry had only two hotel rooms at its disposal. We transformed these two hotel rooms into offices. We had an old, used Golf car and five or six employees. I spoke more than once about how we started collecting paper and pencils in order to draft bills for the Assembly. When the Assembly met, it verified these documents about the appointments of judges and all the other documents and the bills that were passed at the Assembly as laws.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 1D2084, and then we'll go back to this -- and then we'll tender both documents at the same time. 1D2084.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your document, Mr. Minister. Will you please tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Justice, to the MUP of Republika Srpska. It's a request for the use of motor vehicles: "In order to establish the legal system in Republika Srpska as successfully as possible, the Ministry of Justice is duty-bound to contact with the judicial organs on the ground every day. For this, it needs the proper equipment, primarily motor vehicles. Currently, the Ministry of Justice has only one motor vehicle, which is insufficient for it to carry out its work ..." Can we scroll down, please? " ... which is inefficient for it to carry out the jobs and tasks falling within the purview of this organ. "In connection with this, we ask you to provide us and allow us to use three cars, an Audi-type car and two Golf cars. We also ask you to give us an all-terrain vehicle for our use."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the ministry is asking the MUP of Republika Srpska for this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said at the outset, we only had an old Golf.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence, and then we can go back to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D413, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to 65 ter 167, the previous document, to finish with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, while we are waiting for it to come up, will you tell us whether couriers were used, runners, because of the lack of telephone communications?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to avoid repetition, the government or the Ministry of Justice had no material assets, no equipment or funds. We had to start from scratch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2 of this document. Everything you read out here implies the following: Was this the basis for the extended sessions of the Presidency, to which I invited the prime minister and the president of the Assembly so that they could pass on the information and defend their standpoints?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reasons, but I know that the prime minister attended the Presidency sessions and that he informed the Cabinet of what passed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you please read where it says: "The government drew attention to the problem ...," just before "AD-2"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government drew attention to the problem of the information flow among the regions. The Ministry of Traffic and Communications has been tasked with solving this problem as fast as possible."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D414, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, Mr. Karadzic, we'll take a break. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] May we have 168, 65 ter 168.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, these are minutes from the government session of the 3rd of June. How often did the government meet?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government met on a daily basis, if possible; very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's see what it says here. The 3rd of June, the government had a session, just the government; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have the next page, please in English as well, where it says "AD-1," the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The prime minister --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, we're waiting for the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. "The prime minister informed the members of the Cabinet about the current issues of the security situation in the republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, is this what you were referring to when you said that the prime minister informed the members of the Cabinet about what he had learned from other government organs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I won't repeat what I said. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe the procedure here? It says here: "It was concluded that ..." It's the third from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "To start the procedure of establishing war crimes, and this should be done by the War Crimes Commission established by the government," and of another body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We discussed the Documentation Centre, headed by a man of letters. So was it clear that this body was not conducting investigations, but simply keeping the documents?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, war crimes investigated by the regular organs, the Ministry of the Interior and the Commission for War Crimes established by the government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that is a conclusion reached at this government session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is this commission here being tasked only with war crimes against Serbs or is it also tasked with dealing with war crimes committed by Serbs against others?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say here. It just says "war crimes," so this is understood.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't have time to go through the rest of the document, but the document is at the disposal of all parties in full. May it be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to check the accuracy of the interpretation, can I see the -- can we see the first page -- the previous page of this document. Could you read the first sentence in the item "Re. 1," Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the page has to be brought back in the Serbian as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The president of the government --" or "the prime minister informed the members of the Cabinet on the current issues concerning the security situation in the republic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [In English] It should have been "prime minister has informed members of [indiscernible] government."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We understood, Mr. Karadzic. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D415, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 11244, 65 ter 11244.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you remember that as early as April, the government prohibited any buying or selling of real estate?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So let's have a look at this document, which shows that the Crisis Staff, or the War Presidency at Ilidza, asked for clarification from the government. So can you explain to us what the government's response was to the Municipal Assembly of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To the Municipal Assembly of Ilidza. "Hereby we inform you that the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has reviewed your letter regarding occupancy of deserted houses and apartments. "The government considers that citizens whose apartments or houses have been destroyed may obtain only temporary permission to move into deserted houses or apartments. The government will draw up a proposal for a special regulation, based on objective criteria, to find a permanent solution to the issue of providing for citizens whose houses or apartments have been destroyed."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this way, the government is acting to prevent the misuse of abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D416, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now have 1D2074.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for it, I'll ask you the following: Minister, would I be correct in saying that we always counted on Muslims and Croats living among us, and that they would be proportionately represented in our government bodies -- 1D20074, yes, yes, that's it -- and that Muslims and Croats would be proportionately represented in our authorities, just as Serbs should be proportionally represented in the government bodies of Muslim and Bosnian areas?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your ministry, the process of appointing judges and prosecutors, was it conducted in such a way that candidates would be proposed by people on the ground, and you would bring this to the Assembly or to me if the Assembly was unable to meet?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, in the Ministry of Justice, asked the regional centres, and I think there's a letter in the documentation of the OTP or of this honourable Court, to nominate candidates meeting the formal and legal requirements, and to inform us of the ethnic make-up of the regional municipality from which the candidates came, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you describe this document sent to you by the SAO of Semberija and Majevica, the Assembly of the Municipality of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the delivery -- a delivery of the proposal of candidates for judicial bodies in the territory of the municipality of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th of June, 1992, less than a month after my appointment, and for the Basic Court in Bijeljina, the person nominated as president of the Court is Judge Veselin Londrovic, and as judges, Vesna Stevanovic, Mileva Lazarevic, Vera Medan, Dragomir Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just read out the names of those who are not Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. President. Alma Salihbegovic, Alida Nadj-Madjarac, Muhamed Gruhonjic, and Cviko Adamovic, all these were non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. What number is Cviko Adamovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I know that Zvizdic was later appointed, but his name was crossed out here. Could you tell us -- could you read out who the candidates for prosecutors were?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milosevic, Nadezda, in Bijeljina. And the deputies: Dragica Ristic; Vinka Musladin; and Smail Salihbegovic. Dragica is a Serb, and Vinka is a Croat, and Smail is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, this represented the position of the local authorities that are following your instructions regarding proportionate representation; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most regions, in most local communities, there wasn't any particular resistance. But as you know, Mr. President, in some there were -- there was quite a bit of resistance where representatives of certain local organisations were opposed to this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D417.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D2029, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see what happened afterwards. Now, your ministry collects these proposals and send them to the Assembly, or, rather, the president of the republic if the Assembly cannot meet; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 81, paragraph 2 of the Constitution, does it not read that if the Assembly cannot meet, the Presidency or the president of the republic passes a decision, and the MPs then have to confirm it at their next session? If they violated the Constitution, then they have to resign?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is Article 81, paragraph 3 of the Constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read out here who was appointed judge?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among those that we mentioned a moment ago, Dadj-Madjarac, that is, and Zvizdic, Alisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alija?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's barely legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alija Zvizdic, that is the Basic Court in Bijeljina, according to the original proposal; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, could you indicate to the Trial Chamber what this is that we are going through?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are parts of the Official Gazette of the Serb People. It is the Official Gazette -- it is the Official Gazette of the Parliament, or, rather, these are the decisions with the force of law, all the decisions that are made by the Assembly, the Presidency, and the government, and other state organs within their own provinces of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they enter into force once they're published in the Official Gazette; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, eight days after they're published in the Official Gazette, unless stated otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the same number, number 10, dated the 30th of June. Who was appointed in judge in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Selihbegovic, Alija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think it says "Alma."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, my copy is barely legible and I couldn't really see. Alma, yes, Alma.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is Alma, in terms of ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about Trebinje, the Basic Court in Trebinje? Who was appointed there? Actually, I can read it out, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try, Mr. President. Maric, Miroslav, president. And judges are Ljiljana Simovic, Rajko Kozjak, Milan Bosic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They're Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next two?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ehliman Fetahagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ehliman?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Zijad Campara.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What are they, in terms of ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page, please. The next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Karabeglic, Frano, appointed judge in the Higher Court in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franjo has got to be a Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the third page after this one; that is to say, we skipped two and then we move on to the third one after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. This is a decision of the election of judges of the Higher Court in Banja Luka. Now could we have the next page in English as well, please. Minister, can you tell us who it was that was elected judge of the Higher Court in Banja Luka? Who are they; Kresimir, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kresimir, Djukic, is a Croat. Svjetlana Djordjevic Suput, Serb. Branislav Kosic, Serb. Kovacek, Berislav, Croat. Kotlo, Suada, Muslim. Zehra Kerenovic, Muslim. Asim Krupic, Muslim. Strahinja Djurkovic, Serb. Jakl --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Stanislav?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanislav, a Croat. Jeremic, Dusko, a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just scroll down a bit. Adem Medic. Is Adem Medic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have page 2, the second half. Actually, the second half of this same page. So, yes, we'd like to see a different column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Ruzica Topic, what is she by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She's a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Zinaida Kadic, what about her?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian, and probably in English too. The next page in Serbian and -- I see. Could we scroll down a bit, the Serbian page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was appointed deputy prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibrahim Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D418, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have -- actually, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that I signed all of this, instead of the Assembly, at your proposal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and for the most part these proposals of mine, along with your signatures -- or, rather, the decisions you made and signed, the Assembly basically passed these decisions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
