utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D3030 [as interpreted]. 2030, 1D2030. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you give us your comment that relates to Vinka Musladin?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was appointed deputy prosecutor in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that is in accordance with the list that was proposed at local level?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She is an ethnic Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the second column of this same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you give us your comment in this regard, the situation in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salihbegovic, Osman -- Smail, rather, Smail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Salihbegovic, Smail; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Smajl Salihbegovic was appointed deputy public prosecutor in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now scroll down a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gluhonjic, Muhamed is appointed judge of the Basic Court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D419, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Minister, whether this number basically corresponds to the number of Muslims and Croats in Bijeljina? There were very few of them; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the pre-war situation. That is the ratio before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although the war had been on for three months or whatever, you continue with these proposals that reflect the ethnic composition of the population?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pre-war composition or structure, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2063, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the Official Gazette of the Serb People in Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated the 13th of July? Actually, if that was the 10th of June and then the 30th of June and now it's the 13th of July, that means that it's two weeks after that last one?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a bit more than two weeks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at page 18 of this document. Can we scroll down a bit. Can we look at the middle of the second paragraph. We're interested in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this confirms the appointment of Ehliman Fetahagic and Zijad Campara; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is was published in the Official Gazette of the Serb People.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All this took place while I was still signing all of these documents, while the Assembly was not meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what you're supposed to do on the basis of the Constitution when there is an imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D420, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D2061, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, now I am not dealing with things in strictly chronological order. I would like to focus on the subject of the judicial system, and you would be the best person to ask, as far as 1992 is concerned, because you're the person who sent me these proposals; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the Official Gazette dated the 10th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly have page 5 to identify what it is, and then page 6, please. The second half, fine, that will do. No, one page ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what we are interested in, the decision on the election of judges of the Higher Court in Banja Luka. Could you scroll up a bit so that the minister can see 391 in its entirety. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the 10th of August again, and are the decisions on the election of: Djukic, Kresimir, a Croat; Berislav Kovacek, a Croat; Suada Kotlo, a Muslim; Zehra Kerenovic, a Muslim; Asim Krupic, a Muslim; and Medic, Adem, a Muslim? Are they reconfirmed again, just like Zinaida Kadic; are they reconfirmed as judges of the High Court of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ruzica Topic as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ruzica Topic is a Croat lady?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page of this document. Can we just scroll down a bit. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you cast a glance at these deputy public prosecutors in Banja Luka, including Alagic, Ibrahim? I don't know about the rest, whether they're all Serbs, but Ibrahim Alagic is a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification, again, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D421, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we'll translate only the part that was referred to. Are you fine with this, Mr. Tieger? We don't have to translate all the other parts in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that would be unduly burdensome, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That would apply to the Official Gazette we dealt with previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I answered, I guess, in the abstract, Your Honour. But I understand we may have a complete translation for the document you were referring to, so perhaps it's more useful if we confirm the existence, and then the Court can make a decision based on whether or not a translation already exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Items published in the Official Gazette usually are separate matters, I take it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- in the normal course of business, I agree. I mean, it seemed that Dr. Karadzic was interested in this particular section. That would normally be the portion of a document like this, which is segmented in precisely the way the Court indicated, that would be translated. But it did seem fair to let the Court and Dr. Karadzic know that a translation -- full translation was available. But since other separate items of the Gazette don't seem to be at issue, it seems to be not relevant for this purpose at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not clear. You want the entire translation of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had understood that the entire -- that the -- sorry, let me step back. If Dr. Karadzic is tendering just that segment, then I think the answer is clear to everyone. I had understood, however, that it seemed that the entire Gazette was being submitted. I didn't know -- and then I thought the translation issue might be the one obstacle to its admission, so I wanted to alert the Court to the existence of that translation. I'm not suggesting that the remainder -- or that the Gazette should be admitted in its entirety. That seems to be the decision at the moment of the Defence, but I don't have any objections to the admission of such a document, if he's tendering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I take it, Mr. Karadzic, that your position is that you're tendering only the part that you referred to today in this Official Gazette, which is of 36 pages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellency, for reasons of economy, and we are on this subject now and Mr. Mandic was the minister who directly sent this proposal, but the Defence has nothing against all the documents of the government and the Assembly and the Presidency being treated as exhibits on condition that we know that and that we prepare ourselves accordingly. All these documents are at the disposal of all, but for the time being the Defence is happy with just this subject. But when we treat another subject, we will probably be revisiting some other parts of these same Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. We admitted only those parts referred to during the session, and on that -- with that understanding, we'll carry on. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 5587.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until we get it, Mr. Minister, let me ask you this: Do you agree that there were quite a few tensions in the field on account of the arrival of the dead and also because people who lived with us there had their relatives in the adversary's army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the details, but there were quite a few tensions in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Namely, was this a highly-risky action; namely, appointing judges and prosecutors who were Muslims and Croats, while dead people who had been killed by the Muslim and Croatian Army were coming in?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were resistances in some parts of the republic. In fact, even at the Assembly sessions, certain MPs voiced their dissatisfaction at my proposals and the fact that you signed the appointment of certain officials who were non-Serbs. I believe that we have already seen so far that in several instances, some appointments were postponed until talks were held with those who were against such appointments; namely, until the opponents of these proposals were persuaded that that was the right course of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us identify this. This is the 19th Session of the Serbian People, held on the 19th of August, 1992, in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does Momcilo Mandic -- in other words, do you propose here on the first page the inclusion on the agenda the item -- the agenda item of election and appointment of judges in the Lower Court in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked for you to be skipped over and for the Assembly to directly decide on the election of judicial officials.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see page 2032, 0410-2032. That will be perhaps page 14 of this. In the Serbian language, in the top there is an ERN number. One of the experts of the OTP misinterpreted here Mr. Vito Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who is Vitomir Popovic, Mr. Minister?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, he was the president of the Lower Court in Banja Luka, and later he was to become the vice-premier, the vice-prime minister, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is the Serbian page, and in English we have to look for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The discussion surrounds the selection, and some are against the election of judges whose next of kin are somewhere in the enemy's army. And here is what Mr. Popovic says on the topic -- will you interpret this as --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vito Popovic is trying to persuade -- do you want me to read it or to re-tell it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe it is better for you to re-tell it and the participants can read it, if they so like?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vito Popovic as the president of the Lower Court in Banja Luka, which covers a huge territory and quite a few inhabitants; insists that at least 50 per cent of the judges be elected in order for the judicial system to be able to function. And if certain MPs from the Banja Luka region insisted that no non-Serb judges are elected, he proposes that the elections and appointments be postponed. But in order for the judiciary to be able to function -- to elect at least those judges and prosecutors around him, there is no controversy at that session, because there were already quite a few people in detention who needed to be processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the end --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where it says "5 per cent." Towards the end of the Serbian version, before that, one sentence before that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise: "It should be stated that then in talking with representatives of the Ministry of Justice of our republic, we agreed to go ahead with the election on national structure basis, but that that number should be considerably reduced. Bearing in mind the ethnic representation, we propose that there should be 5 per cent of judges of other ethnicity."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We agree that Mr. Popovic did not want to discuss, on a political basis, the respective shares, but insisted that at least those around whom there was no dispute be elected immediately so that the cases which were pending could be processed; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 16 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now the MPs are voting, and it is quite a fight. Can you tell us what the number 13 is about? That is 2036. In the Serbian language, it was 2032, and now it is four pages further, 2036. One page before that, 13.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Zoran Lipovac, a Croat," is under number 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Read it, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Who is in favour? We have to count. It seems that we all are. Two against. And I know that Zoran Lipovac has been elected."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the one under him, below?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also a Croat, but he was not elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Boris Markovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Who is in favour? Who is against? All. Any abstentions? Two. I know that Boris Markovic has not been elected judge."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see the next page in Serbian and page 18 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We see that some were not elected, and that was as a result of the resistances offered. And in view of the fact that one Croat was elected and the other one was not, these resistances were not motivated ethnically, but rather were on a personal basis?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I have testified in respect of this topic very extensively in the Stanisic case, when Ms. Korner examined me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the Serbian version, 2038; in other words, the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "In view of the fact that some were elected, whereas others were not, this is my intervention, and would you be so kind as to read that intervention of mine, and after that, the response to that of Mr. Krajisnik, the Assembly president.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Dr. Karadzic: I believe I need to say something not only about this proposal, but about the principle of the matter, if I may. Look, as we have said yesterday, we have to see whether he or she is an appropriate person. But as far as other nations are concerned, we have to have a percentage, a proportion, consistent with that in the municipal authorities. We have to be responsible. We are creating a state. You are the organ creating it. The state must be created swiftly and well. It has to have all its elements in order to survive and to remain as a state."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And because it is able to, it should make it of all its ingredients."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I mean is because the Serbian people is capable of doing that, it should compose its state of all its ingredients and elements. What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the national mix should be adequate at all levels of authority in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this contribution of mine, because this was your department?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I remember that some MPs from the Krajina actually attacked you on that score.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read what the presiding -- the president, actually Mr. Krajisnik, said?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The president: Radovan, let me explain. Nobody rejects them because they are not good or because they are Muslims or Croats. Simply, the policy is such that we have to make our options now because we are in a state of civil war. They will lose this number of judges, and when the war is over they will be -- when the conditions are created, they will be elected."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this actually show that when the conditions are created -- when adequate conditions are created, when the fighting dies down, et cetera, that there will be elections?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, Mr. Krajisnik's position was that we should talk to those MPs who withheld their consent for members who were non-Serbs -- for non-Serbs to be elected to these offices and for the Assembly to be prepared, in a way, to respect the ethnic mix of the different regions and have it reflected adequately in the judicial system, in the offices within the judicial system.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be adopted -- admitted? I believe that it has been admitted in toto as a transcript, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It hasn't been admitted, to my knowledge. We'll admit it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D422, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice, Minister, when I'm asking for the floor, I'm asking if I may say, which indicates that the Assembly is a body independent of the president of the republic and it's the legislative branch of authority?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any way for the president to impose on the Presidency his opinion or an arrangement?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Assembly, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to 65 ter 30413.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe this is the intercepted conversation between me and Mr. Kupresanin of 9 November 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Vojo Kupresanin we discussed before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read this line where I say: "Please"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Radovan Karadzic: Please, nobody approached me, and nobody got permission from me to change the decision of the Assembly. I don't have that right. Nobody has the right to change it."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this consistent with your knowledge that the president of the republic honoured the Assembly as the highest legislative body in the country?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we MFI this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D423.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 30519. Sorry, 30591. It was a slip of the tongue. That's it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is already in February of 1992, the 10th of February. Again, Kupresanin and Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 4 in Serbian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the bottom, it says: "Please ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Radovan Karadzic: Come on. It's not just the smarts. There are also obligations. One of our MPs, he's the supreme authority in the Assembly of the Serbian People, and when the Assembly of the Serbian People decide something, Brdo cannot do any different. He cannot. And if he does do any different, he's not loyal, he's doing the work of a traitor, whether he likes it or not. I cannot -- no longer continue to be such a great democrat as to tolerate this, because he can do real damage. If he couldn't, I wouldn't care."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this also part of the struggle for democratic decisions to be enforced, and I should have even been firmer than I actually was, more adamant?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you rephrase that question to make it a bit clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this intercept reflect that I was fighting for democratically-made decisions to be implemented, and that I should have perhaps been even more adamant in this effort?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only note that you are trying to prevail upon Vojo Kupresanin that the man in question had to abide by the Assembly's decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "I can no longer be such a great democrat as to tolerate this." Was I responsible for the enforcement of decisions taken in such a democratic way?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the president of the party or the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's 1992 already, but it's before the outbreak of the war, and I'm co-ordinating the work of the party. Am I responsible for the implementation of decisions that had been taken in a democratic way?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only read this as your effort to persuade the MPs that they had to honour the decisions of the Assembly, whereas one person here - what was his name? - Vukic or something, he is refusing to abide by these decisions made by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree that I'm considering the Assembly as the supreme authority?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we get 65 ter 01000. Was this document before MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think so. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D424, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I now ask you to look at this document, which is accompanied this time by a translation, this passage where Radovan Karadzic says: "Ladies and gentlemen ...," but in English it would be page 2. From the words: "We hope ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We hope that the representatives are getting more active in municipalities, because as we concluded last time, a representative is an authority for us, the party ... parties are a service to the elected people, the people, and to people elected by the people to carry out the political will of the people. Party officials are not the authority."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The authority for us are primarily MPs, representatives, and the rest."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this also confirm that the party provides a service? It cannot govern; it only helps the elected organs and officials to exercise the power given them by the people in the elections?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are explaining here that the representatives in the Assembly and deputies in local parliaments are the people who are exercising power, the people who govern in the branches of power to which they were elected.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 1 just to identify this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an extended session, that is, a plenary session, of the main and executive boards of the SDS, held on 19 February 1992 in the Holiday Inn Hotel. Do you agree that the Main Board cannot be expanded, just a session can be expanded by including additional people?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the statute of the party, so I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I meant the Presidency. If a presidency is holding an expanded session, that doesn't mean that the Presidency, itself, has expanded; it just invited guests and observers and other people to attend the session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'd like to object to that. First of all, I don't know what kind of opinion Dr. Karadzic is seeking from this witness, because we've strayed from this document to an expert opinion on the Main Board about which this witness claims not to have expertise, and now we're moving on to the Presidency and an opinion about that. So -- and that's from Mr. Mandic, who assured me he didn't want to testify as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, but I remember having heard from the witness as to the meaning of the extended sitting -- expanded session. But let's carry on, Mr. Karadzic. But on a separate note, I was wondering why this document was titled as "Intercept."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's a recording, Your Honour. I think -- I don't think it should be -- I agree it's not -- obviously, it's not a telephone conversation, and so to that extent it would seem to be a misleading designation. But I think it's somehow tied to the fact that it's a recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as the Presidency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was informed that part of this exhibit has already admitted as P12, so this will be added to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman is a lawyer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just going to say in keeping with -- this is a session of the Deputy's Club, very closely linked to the Assembly. I would think in keeping with the approach that we've adopted recently, it might make more sense to have this session tendered in its entirety rather than keep accumulating excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's 30 pages now. We'll admit it in its entirety, unless it is objected to. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll change the P12 to compose of every document, if that's feasible by the Registry. With that understanding, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English page 10, please. While we're waiting, I just wanted to say that Mr. Mandic has a degree in law and he knows how the Presidency may be changed; only by constitutional amendment. This is a plenary session of the party, which we see that representatives of municipal boards and others have been invited to attend. That's what the plenary session --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The plenary session is a general session, as it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian, it's 203 [as interpreted]. The one we had now was 2217, and we now need 2203.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the bottom, it says: "Another problem that cropped up ...," below "Vukic," below the name "Vukic."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Another problem that cropped up is that the power is alienated from the party. That's a catastrophic problem. We can't allow for that. Presidents of municipalities, presidents of the executive boards, some, at least, not all, do not care much for MPs, and they should. Their MP is the supreme authority in their locality. He's part of the highest supreme body, and he's a member of the Serbian Assembly of the common Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "He is a member of the largest authority and a member of the Serbian Assembly, and he is also part of the Municipal Representatives Club."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get page 20 now. English page 20 and Serbian page 2211.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read the part where it says: "500.000 Serbs, that's not the exercise of rights by the people. A million people remain outside Krajina, and we have to agree amongst ourselves."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We have to agree. If this policy is no good, then the Main Board has to decide so today, that it's no good, that it's leading into a dead-end, that so far not a single objective has been attained, and then let's change the leadership."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see the next page, and you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It will, it will. I will be grateful. You will not accept me. Will you give me a decoration or something. I will be an honorary member or something, because I was the first president of the party, and I'll be happy and grateful to move forward with the new policy. If there is an alternative policy and you are offering it, and we are not implementing it, then we deserve to be replaced."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go a bit further down?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The supreme body of power of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina is the Serbian Assembly. Make no mistake about that."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at this time, the Bosnia-Herzegovina Conference has been underway for quite a while, presided by Mr. Cutileiro?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the month of February, when the Cutileiro Plan was being implemented and when the Sarajevo Agreement and the Lisbon Agreement were topical.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of this document has been admitted, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that both as the president of the party, even without any state office, and later as president of the republic, I am trying to get decisions made by the Assembly implemented, I'm trying not to allow anyone to change them willfully?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see in this text, you have a problem with Brdjanin and some other MPs, and you are trying to prevail upon them that they have to be part of the Serbian Assembly and part of the Joint Assembly, and that they have to work to implement the decisions made by the Assembly majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It wasn't recorded, but I'd like you to confirm or deny that I wasn't always successful in pushing my proposals.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. More than once your proposals were not accepted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D192, could I have that now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a topic that we dealt with, creating a state based on rule of law, creating a judicial system on that basis, then our struggle in the Assembly and in the field to have this carried through. Now let us see how the state organs are operating, apart from all of our interventions. Can you tell us who Mr. Dobro Planojevic is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobro Planojevic is a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He is not politically involved, he's not a member of the SDS; he is a policeman inside-out; is that it, in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobro Planojevic was a police cadet in Vraca and had joined the police force when he was 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this bear the date of the 8th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I remind you that I issued an order that we already discussed about observing international norms and the Geneva Conventions on the 13th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, as you said, perhaps that was necessary for the sake of authority in the area. However, let us have a look at this. Did state organs act that way, even without that? So can you please read this, this part that starts with: "Over the past two months ...," et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Over the past two months, since the war broke out in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, there has been a considerable increase in the commission of crimes, property-related crimes, war profiteering --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 18395.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we then have both versions on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you wish, have a look at this, and then interpret it for us. You don't really need to read out the entire text, because the participants can do that on their own.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobro Planojevic is informing the CSB of Banja Luka, as assistant minister for crime-related affairs. He is speaking about war profiteering and other crimes, and also the commission of war crimes, and he is asking for persons who committed war crimes to be handed over to the judiciary or the military police. He is also asking for documentation of criminal activity, as he says, both of groups and individuals, and also he's demanding their urgent arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on. What else does he say? He is also drawing attention to what? That's the second part.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Inter alia, could corpses be photographed and, wherever possible, post-mortems, because in these wartime conditions you will encounter many obstacles in your battle against crime, and you will sometimes be unable to take adequate measures. In such cases, all findings should be properly recorded in the form of official notes so that necessary measures or criminal prosecution could be taken subsequently."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you continue?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We take this opportunity to emphasise that the civilian population and prisoners of war should be treated in strict compliance with the regulations of international law of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then there is his signature, and what does Stojan Zupljanin add to this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that. Could you scroll down a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you scroll down a bit. I believe it's the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "It is necessary for all authorised officials of the Public Security Service to be familiarised with the content of this dispatch and to observe the instructions from this dispatch in your further activities." Signed by chief of centre, Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you know that to this day in Bosnia-Herzegovina, proceedings are underway on the basis of criminal reports that were filed by our organs during the war?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is still underway, but I know that proceedings were carried out for a long time on the basis of these reports, considerably after the crimes were committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this set of instructions of Dobro Planojevic, namely, that if you cannot prosecute, then provide proper documentation and matters will be dealt with later? Was that actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the Muslim area in Bihac, Serbs are being tried on the basis of our criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then on some other occasion, we are going to show these judgements that are based on our criminal reports. Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, whose document is this? Is this document signed by Planojevic, or Mr. Zupljanin, or by both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of Dobro Planojevic, assistant minister for crime prevention. And the amendment is written by Stojan Zupljanin. That is to say, he said that that document needs to be observed in terms of further activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who was in a higher position, in terms of hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Dobro Planojevic was the first-ranking. He informed by a dispatch the chief of the centre of security Services in the area of Banja Luka who is lower ranking but encompasses a number of security stations in some ten municipalities. But Dobro Planojevic, as the high-ranking, gave these instructions to the chief. He then passed on these instructions to all his subordinates that they should act in accordance with instructions of Dobro Planojevic; namely, he lowered it to the municipal level, to the field level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If it is convenient, we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, just to clarify, just one sentence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the central authorities, a dispatch was sent to the region and from the regional level to the municipal level, to the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we will admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D425, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Twenty-five minutes. We'll resume at 10 to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. [Interpretation] May I have 1D191, please. 1D191.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this, Minister, let me ask you whether the police was duty-bound to report to me about their regular activities if they had no special problem.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they reported to the government, or, rather, the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please cast a glance at this, then, further down. It's the 8th of June, isn't it? And you can perhaps tell the Trial Chamber and all the participants what this actually is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 01083, Your Honour, will enable us to find a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have both version on the screen, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We don't need to read out every word, but could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what this is, especially the five points?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the Serb agency "SRNA," you are addressing all the relevant factors in the Government of the Republika Srpska. Number 1, you are asking all the local authorities and prominent individuals of Serb ethnicity to ensure protection and care for all wounded and ill individuals, regardless of which side they belong to. What they mean here is which warring party they belong to. Also, to humanely treat all persons. Also, that the civilian population be spared of all attacks. Also, to provide protection and all possible aid to refugees and to respect the Red Cross sign and to use that sign only for markings on medical personnel, hospitals and ambulances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the last -- the last sentence. And it's the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We are renewing our call for the resumption of the activities of the International Red Cross and the protection of all civilians of all nations, as well as prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since communications were down, was this perhaps the only way to send the positions of the state authorities to all parts of the country? Was anything else possible?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anything else was possible, but I know that at the beginning of the war, all communications were down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D426, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 171, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a government session held on the 8th of June; isn't that right, Minister?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have all the participants focus on this. Now we'd like to look at page 2 in both languages, I think. Do you agree that there are no more government sessions held together with the National Security Council; there is not a single such case once there was a normal Assembly life?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It was concluded that during the course of the day, the ministries should prepare a questionnaire on the basis of which the situation in the field could be examined so as to provide --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "For uniformity"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... uniformity and insight into the real situation in the municipalities, that the regulation on apartments should be prepared immediately, that is, the regulations about moving Serb people who are left without accommodation into deserted houses and flats. Among other things, the regulations should state that temporary decrees should be issued as soon as possible; that before moving in, a committee should make a list of all property; and that the property and facilities should be taken care of," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the government still have to deal with the situation in which they don't know what is happening in the municipalities, the municipalities are practically state-lets in their own right, and does it state here that all property has been recorded by these commissions or committees and only temporarily made available for the use of other persons; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this was the situation that made it necessary to establish the Office of Commissioners of the Central Authorities so that they could tour municipalities and inform them of what was going on, and also they should inform the government about what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, that was one of the reasons why crisis staffs were supposed to be dismantled.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D427, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 114.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I tell you that this is yet another expanded meeting of the War Presidency. It's not the War Presidency, actually, because we haven't declared a state of war. And it is held on the 9th of June, so can we identify this, and then could you look at that first and second paragraph, General Mladic and General Gvero?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meeting was held on the 9th of June, 1992, and General Mladic briefed the Presidency in detail about the overall situation in the Serb Army, and he presented figures on the quantities of weapons, ammunition, spare parts, reserves of oil and oil products, food and other reserves: "General Gvero reported on the situation in the area of the Banja Luka Corps and proposed that authorities be established at all levels swiftly because of the widespread crimes."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that all heavy artillery activities should be stopped and that a strong unit should be sent to help the units around Sarajevo? Now I'd like to ask you whether you agree that our supremacy, in terms of the number of weapons, was the only such element in terms of the balance of strategic forces around Sarajevo? I mean, I am trying --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot follow this, and I did not know what the situation in the army was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm putting to you: Since a decision is being made to stop the use of artillery, it is stated in paragraph 4 that a unit has to come from Krajina in order to keep the situation as it is, in terms of the Serb neighbourhoods, because if there would be an exclusion of heavy artillery, they would beat us. So that is why this unit had to come from Krajina, if there is an exclusion of heavy artillery; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a meeting of the expanded War Presidency. These are minutes from that meeting, and I can only interpret this on the basis of what you've just put to me. I, personally, was not aware of the military situation around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree that -- oh, all right, we're not going to deal with that subject. Do you agree that in the beginning of June, the young people of Pale got killed in Zepa after a deception of the municipal authorities of the Muslims in Zepa? They had promised them safe passage, and then they killed all of them. Was there a funeral held at Pale?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that incident because there was a big funeral of all these young people at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Such mass funerals of Serb fighters, did they aggravate tensions and did they lead to fear amongst the Muslim population? Do you know about that or -- and is that only natural?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when things like this happened, of course, the other side was afraid that there would be revenge, and there was fear on all three sides that were at war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read out what we decided; paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 6: "That mass burials of dead soldiers be banned and condolences to their families be expressed in a dignified way."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is some information here about how the airport was handed over and so on, but could you please read 11?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Write up instructions for the Serb Army to observe the Geneva Conventions when treating prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the 9th of June, and my order was issued on the 13th of June; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that when there was a lack of communication and there were hardly any media, this had nothing to do with propaganda; this was a substantive matter?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was life, itself, at the seat of the Government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D428, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 172, that's the 65 ter number I'd like to have now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this document minutes from the government meeting held on the same day as the Presidency session?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read 1(a)?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Order of the Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then under AD-1, "Re-1," under A?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government has supported the text of the order of the Central Commission for the Exchange of the Prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the commission was a government organ and we can see from this that it also issued orders?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued by the Central Commission and it was signed by Mr. Colovic. And as we have noted already, the Central Commission was a government organ, a body, a governmental body.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under B, can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government acknowledged the letter of the president of the Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners. It was concluded that the minister of justice should conduct a talk with Rajko Colovic, the president of the commission, to establish what the motives are for asking for a replacement, and that if reasons for dismissal are justified, the above-named shall continue to perform the duty of president of commission until a new president of the commission is appointed."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now: "The government has noted ..." Can you just re-tell us that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, as I've said in my testimony in the Stanisic case, and I fully stand by what I said then, the observed problem -- the problem with the exchange of prisoners appeared throughout the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the government set up an independent governmental body which had the power to set up regional and municipal commissions which were under it. The lists were to be centralised so there would be comprehensive informing on both warring sides. Mr. Rajko Colovic was elected, I believe, at the proposal of the prime minister, and the other two members were from the line ministries. I think one was from the Ministry of the Interior, and the Ministry of Justice, and I'm not sure which other ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it's stated here that these were delicate matters, that instructions should be prepared to incorporate international regulations, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've just said so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this has been admitted as Exhibit P1091.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 11024.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, this is Exhibit P1090.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent. Then we do not have to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is from the 6th of June, 1992, the Central Commission for the Exchange of Captured Persons, and it is stated here "Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Central Commission." It is not considered to be under the government at all, but it is an independent body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that this was an independent governmental body. I've said so -- that many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What remains unclear here, and it has been presented by the Prosecution -- can we see the next page, in fact? Can we see the next page in Serbian, too? What remains unclear is the situation or the fate of able-bodied -- can I ask you to focus on this part which begins with: "Svezene" [phoen] up to the part with "legislation and captives"? Can you read that part and interpret it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All women whose prisoners -- who are prisoners --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm sorry, but the interpreter is unable to find the corresponding paragraph in English, or in Serbian, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So first we need to find out the passage in the document, and if you could repeat reading again. But for the benefit of the interpreters, Mr. Karadzic, could you identify the passage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the fourth paragraph from the top, and in the English version, it is the last passage on this side which we now -- on this page which we now see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "All women whose captivity, either deprivation of freedom, is not associated with war operations so is not connected to war operations, children and minors up to 16 years old, old, infirm, and sick persons, should be immediately released and ensured safe movement according to their expressed wishes, without any conditions being set to them or exchanges."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but this is not the right English page. It is now there, which starts with "All women ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, on what grounds could somebody be arrested if they were not prisoners of war? Were there any other grounds for arresting people?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was part of the regular, routine criminal procedure. If someone was suspected of having committed a crime, they would be -- that would be grounds for their arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you read this paragraph or interpret it for us, the one which says: "All persons ..." [In English] "All persons have to be granted ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All persons have to be ensured freedom of movement, of removal according to their wishes, if that does not mean jeopardising personal or general safety."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Persons taken prisoners and persons deprived of liberty, against whom criminal proceedings have been instituted, shall not be subject of this order, but the provisions of the Criminal Code shall be applicable."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it depends on the actual criminal offence, what shall be applicable. Can I now ask you, Mr. Minister, whether our law distinguishes between domicile and address, and can you explain the difference?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Domicile or permanent address is where someone is permanently residing, whereas an address, a place of residence, is a place where someone is registered and stays for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it is where a person stays for a longer time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where a person stays for a longer time and where all his documents are; of the person in question, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that there is something wrong in the -- actually, the domicile is the permanent resident; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And temporary residence or temporary address is where one stays on a temporary basis; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am currently temporarily residing in The Hague, and my permanent residence is in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if someone is asking for the change of a temporary residence, does this mean moving out on a permanent basis or is this just a temporary, interim relocation of the person in question?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is temporary relocation, so temporary residence is a temporary category, and it is delineated in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This has already been admitted, and we need not deal with it any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Mandic, could you read that passage again for us which starts with: "All women ...," which you read some minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "All women -- all women whose detention or deprivation of liberty is not related to war or war activities, and children and minors up to 16 years of age, old, and infirm persons, should be released immediately and their safe movement enabled, according to their expressed wishes, without any conditions being set or any exchange."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to this passage, you were asked by

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "On what grounds could somebody be arrested if they were not prisoners of war? Were there any other grounds for arresting people?" And your answer was: "Well, this was part of the regular, routine criminal procedure. If someone was suspected of having committed a crime, they would be -- that would be grounds for their arrest." Then I would like to ask you: On what grounds were these women arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this order can be explained much better by Mr. Colovic, I'm sure. But in my personal opinion, this was sheltering civilians -- relocating civilians from war-ravaged areas, where there was fighting going on between the warring sides, such as was Dobrinja, for instance, at which time civilians and women and children were placed in certain facilities until the end of the war operations. And the instruction was that after that and in similar situations, those people should be immediately released, naturally, unless they were -- they featured in some other regular criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the thing is that these women were not arrested or detained in relation to war crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, in my interpretation, Your Honours, the way I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we can take it there were at the time also some males, men, who were detained for the same reason as these women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And according to this order, they were not released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to this order, only released unconditionally were women and children and old and infirm people, whereas able-bodied men fit for battle were not released, according to the order of the president of the state commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to explain this "unconditionally"? What was the condition for releasing these people as well, or what was the decisive factor whether they would be released or held?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Able-bodied males were examined by the competent organs, whether civilians or military; namely, by the police or by the military police. And if they hadn't violated the war of law [as interpreted] or had not participated in the fighting or had not been active in the conflicts, they would be released and/or exchanged, whereas these categories that the President of this honourable Court has asked me about, i.e., the Chamber, had to be released without any conditions, without any investigations, without any examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with the assessment of the Muslim General Divjak that in the first year of the war, at least 75 to 80 per cent of them waged war in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know -- actually, I don't know the exact percentage, but I do know that quite a few of the members of the Muslim Army in Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that taking captive someone in the zone of war actions, if someone does not have a uniform, that does not mean that that someone is not a combatant?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was investigated by the competent security services. It was up to them to establish whether someone had participated in the fighting, whether it was an active combatant who participated in the fighting or a civilian who just happened to be in his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall deal with this topic at some length, but let me ask you this: Did you know that in Prijedor and Sanski Most, the authorities had aired on radio an invitation -- a call to civilians to remain at their homes until the fighting against the terrorists was over, and one witness has confirmed that here in respect of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, that prompts me to ask you this: Do you know that from the report that the government asked for, of those captured in Sanski Most, 41 per cent were released and 59 were sent to Manjaca, whereas in Prijedor over 50 per cent were released in this screening, in this triage?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We shall see the relevant documents. Has this document been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We were told it has already been admitted as Prosecution Exhibit 1090.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see 65 ter 01581.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this has been admitted as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Admitted as ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm mistaken. I think I have the wrong 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, is this contract an agreement on the mutual release of prisoners on the principle "all for all"? Tell me who drew this up, who signed it, and when.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This agreement was made by the authorised representatives of the Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of Wars on the basis of an agreement signed on the -- concluded on the 5th of July, 1992. It was signed by Nenad Vanovac on behalf of the Serbian side --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the English, the entire page in English, please. Scroll up a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The 65 ter number of the document we are looking at is 01581, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the number I called, and I received what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then the Registrar should be right. It has already been admitted as Exhibit P1131?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Bikel [phoen] has signed here for the UNPROFOR as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Filip Vukovic signed for the federation side, the Muslim side, and Nenad Vanovac signed for the Serbian side, the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no gender distinction here. All persons found detained on both sides are unconditionally released?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I tried to explain during the examination conducted by Mr. Tieger. I tried to explain this contract.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page; in English as well. No, one page further in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read item 3?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an agreement between you and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, president of the Presidency, concerning an exchange "all for all," and in item 3 it says: "The parties to the agreement accept that the civilian population, especially the old, the infirm, and the sick, women and children, be released unconditionally from detention and captivity through the commission."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is, therefore, underlined that civilian population, that means men, women and children, and especially the old and the infirm; not only the old and infirm, but especially them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assumption here, Mr. President, is that if there are people on both sides in captivity and in detention, including children and the old and the infirm, they should be released immediately, because we had already noted that in certain localities, the crisis staffs kept in captivity old and infirm people. That was before the central authorities and the central state commission was established.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you read to us the last item, 8 -- the last sentence of item 8? The last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The parties to the agreement undertake not to arrest civilians and to enable them to move freely on the territory under their control."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there is no distinction between men and women among civilians?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. All civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see paragraph 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you look at 17, do you agree that for a while, Mr. Izetbegovic signed a separate copy so that his signature would not find itself on the same page as the signature of a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at item 17.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At meetings where they considered the implementation of this agreement, the parties to the agreement shall, without fail, invite representatives of the UNHCR and the UNPROFOR, as well as representatives of the Red Cross of the Serbian Republic BH, the Red Cross of the Republic of BH, and representatives of the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would it have been much less hard on the civilians if this agreement had been honoured?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since this one is admitted, is the Karadzic/Izetbegovic agreement also admitted?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it has already been entered as Exhibit P1131.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2059. I don't know whether we have a translation. If there is one, the Prosecution would know. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that this is the Banja Luka Commission, a regional commission?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report from 1993, from October 1993, when Mr. Vitomir Popovic was the deputy prime minister, and late Jovo Rosic was the minister of justice, and this is, indeed, a regional commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the paragraph 1 say: "Our demand has been accepted to enable the temporary removal or relocation of all Serbs from that area who so wish"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Our demand to enable temporary relocation of all Serbs from that area who so wish has been accepted. In exchange, the Muslims want unhindered passage for convoys of humanitarian aid through to Travnik and Zenica," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what else?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that the Serbs account for 15 to 20 per cent in this convoy, and other ethnicities, Croat, Muslims, Jews, Slovenes, and Macedonians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is it the case that Serbs want to have their population allowed to -- I am sorry. Interpreters, I will repeat. Does this mean that this commission is asking that Serbs from Zenica, Travnik, and Central Bosnia, at least those who so wish, be enabled to move to Serb territory, whereas Muslims set a condition; that humanitarian aid convoys pass unhindered to Travnik and Zenica, and that in the Serbian convoy, there should be 15 to 20 per cent of their own people, Muslims and Croats, who want to go to Europe?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first sentence of paragraph 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that: "In December 1993, a high-ranking Serbian judge/cleric opened three offices for Serbs who want temporary relocation to apply."
