Therefore, it was well known that at that time in Central Bosnia, there was a base there of the Mujahedin, a brigade, El Mujahid, who were especially cruel, and there were many Serbs who fell victim in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the day before Christmas, 6 January 1994, we admitted -- we took in 198 persons from Zenica, including 180 Serbs. The rest are Muslims who are living in third countries (Austria, Germany, Sweden, Slovakia)." Out of them, only one three-member family is purely Muslim. The others are all mixed, including, for instance, family Mitrovic, Trkulja family and Derberovic [phoen], Nedzad, with wife, Gordana, and children, Sasa and Zlatan."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All who came out were temporarily put up in a make-shift admission centre in Ljubija, where they were processed as due. Unfortunately, 14 persons from the Muslim group are still in Ljubija."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean they were waiting for something?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D429.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, can we see the date of this document? The 26th of January, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 24, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that's a report for 1993, because this was the beginning of the year?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Have we got a number for this? Can we go to 65 ter 189.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Same topic. The 41st session of the government, held on 22 July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read to us 7 and 8?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "7. Proposal to appoint the president of the Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War. "8. Agreement on the condition and procedure of exchanging prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then after item 14, you noted that it would be a good idea for more ministers to attend, rather than send their representatives, but it was still found that there was a quorum. Now, can we move four pages forward. In Serbian, the ERN ends with 452. That's perfect. Can you see "AD-8"? And if we could get it in English, it would be probably page 6. Now, could you read number 8?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government upheld the agreement on the conditions and procedure for exchanging prisoners of war. "It has been proposed to refer to the peace agreement recently signed in London in the introductory part of the agreement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that I undertook, before Lord Carrington, that there would be an exchange "all for all" and that civilians would be able to move to a territory that is safer for them, and that was the basis of that agreement which also provided for police escort to civilians up to that territory they wanted to reach?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you rephrase?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that in July -- I do beg the interpreters' pardon. I am under great time pressure. Do you recall that conference in July? It was still the Cutileiro-Carrington Conference. We undertook to exchange prisoners "all for all" and to provide police escort to civilians who wanted to move to another territory they found safer, and that was the basis for some of my orders.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was with the mediation of Lord Carrington, the British negotiator/mediator. I know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, AD-14, third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read to us the third paragraph in 14?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government has been informed about certain incidents of unlawful treatment of prisoners of war. It has been decided to take measures to ensure a consistent implementation of the order by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic BH on the treatment of prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that order, but let me ask you: If the government had criminal intentions, wouldn't it be pleased by this, rather than taking measures to redress the situation? Was the government supporting these incidents of unlawful conduct or not?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian government never had criminal intent, especially not the government where I was a member.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this document admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think -- so we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D430, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we get 65 ter 144.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This a session of the Presidency held on 9 October. You are still on the Cabinet, but Mrs. Plavsic and I were not present. This was just a consultation. Proposals were made, and I later signed those things that were accepted. Can you read to us from the paragraph that begins: "It is noted ..."?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It is noted that an exchange of prisoners did not happen, because the opposite side brought all men and women to be exchanged. Then even the exhumations had not been done. A new meeting was scheduled."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the opposing side often sabotaged exchanges, or they brought an inadequate number of the wounded, or they brought their civilians to be exchanged for fighting men?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there had been problems with exchange of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2014, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We discussed this a moment ago, Minister. It's about civilians in combat areas, combat zones. Let's see what the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps says about this. Sladoje Cedomir signed on his behalf, and that's his chief of staff, I suppose. It's the 22nd of October, 1992. Could you give us a short reading?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps orders: "Women, children and old people from places that are not loyal to our government should be secured on territories of municipalities of their previous residence of organisation -- in the organisation of civilian authorities, enabling correct treatment, safety," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this an order to all units?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's addressed to the commanders of all the units belonging to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read the preamble?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In view of the fact that there have been cases when women, children, and elderly men of Muslim ethnicity were rounded up and sent to the corps command, where they pose an additional burden in terms of accommodation, food and care, and in order to provide organised treatment in the future, I hereby order:"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 2?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Prisoners captured in combat should be sent to the corps command, while taking care that all measures for their safety are taken during the journey. After their processing by officials from the corps command, they will be placed in the Kula Prison, where they would be handed over for further treatment to police officials and commissions for exchange."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 3?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3: "Muslims who remain loyal should be provided with all the necessary conditions for continued life and work, to the extent of our possibilities."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now about these people, were they just -- were they arrested or were they removed from combat zones?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were removed from combat zones and taken to shelters; for instance, to the shelter in the Lukavica Barracks, where there was accommodation and food available.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D432, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, do we have time for another document? 1D2015, 1D2015.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you like to give us a summary of this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from the Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces, and it's sent to all the district defence staffs and all the prisons in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's an order pursuant to international conventions on the treatment of prisoners of war. "1 --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "1. For all persons who are elderly, sick, and women who found themselves in prisons without having committed any crimes or without being suspected of any crimes, immediately provide lists to the State Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners and the Republic Staff of the Supreme Command in order to conduct an organised exchange in agreed places, under the supervision and control of the Republic Commission," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This position they take towards the sick, the elderly, the women, et cetera, is it same as our position, our altitude towards these people? Did they bring them to be exchanged? And if they did, did we do the same?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, Mr. President, but I do know that there were problems with exchanges, and the presidents of these commissions, the Regional and the Central Commission, were more familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this signed by Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first commander of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this, by definition, rule out able-bodied fighting men or men fit for the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does mean that elderly people, sick people, and women were detained in the territory held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they were subject to exchange?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It could be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D433, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that may be it for today. Yes. Again, we'll sit in the afternoon tomorrow, 2.15. Have a nice evening.
